source_hypotheses.required: Modular elliptic curve over Q with analytic rank at most1.
source_hypotheses.constructed: A/Q is the elliptic curve in the forward-rank lemma; modularity is supplied separately by BCDT.
source_hypotheses.justification: The final theorem has no residual-image condition or prime exclusion; BCDT final-source review remains separate.

constructed_objects.required: The usual elliptic L-function at s=1, Mordell-Weil rank and the full localization-kernel Sha.
constructed_objects.constructed: The manuscript uses those same objects before passing to the2-primary Kummer sequence.
constructed_objects.justification: Published p429 defines Sha with all places; p430 fixes L and analytic rank.

index_domain_coverage.required: Every modular elliptic curve over Q in analytic ranks0 or1.
index_domain_coverage.constructed: The entire family in the lemma is covered, since each curve is modular and its assumed analytic rank is at most1.
index_domain_coverage.justification: The inclusive inequality was checked in the actual printed page, not OCR alone.

transition_maps.required: Auxiliary-field restriction if the explanatory proof chain is used.
transition_maps.constructed: The manuscript restricts Sha(Q) to Sha(K) and retains its finite2-torsion kernel.
transition_maps.justification: Published p431 explicitly gives this containment; no isomorphism between the two Sha groups is asserted.

consumed_object_identity.constructed: Exactly A(Q) and Sha(A/Q) enter the Kummer sequence.
consumed_object_identity.justification: Theorem1 directly supplies the Q-result; Theorems3-5 explain the auxiliary route and do not replace the final object.

coefficient_conventions.required: Integral group rank and finiteness of the entire Sha.
coefficient_conventions.constructed: The downstream corank is over Z2 after tensoring A(Q) by Q2/Z2.
coefficient_conventions.justification: Finite Sha contributes zero corank, so the corank equals the same integral rank.

local_conditions.required: Modular parametrization X0(N) to A; the full Sha at every place.
local_conditions.constructed: N is the conductor, and BCDT supplies the modularity input.
local_conditions.justification: The theorem is global; it requires no ordinary or good reduction at2.

exceptional_cases.required: Both analytic ranks0 and1; no higher-rank conclusion.
exceptional_cases.constructed: The lemma assumes r at most1; all later uses are in this range.
exceptional_cases.justification: Neither the cited theorem nor this replacement establishes a converse or the restricted2-converse.

downstream_consumption.required: Forward rank and finiteSha for the two curves after the restricted converse.
downstream_consumption.constructed: The pole-completeness argument consumes rank1 and finiteSha after applying RC.
downstream_consumption.justification: Only the citation edition and page locator change. RC and all other inputs stay independently pending as applicable.

source_hypotheses.required: Abelian p-adic representation of a finite local extension, Hodge-Tate with semisimple inertia.
source_hypotheses.constructed: Base field Q5, finite coefficient field E, one-dimensional E-valued deRham character.
source_hypotheses.justification: Restriction of scalars is Hodge-Tate; multiplication in E diagonalizes after scalar extension, including on inertia.

constructed_objects.required: Finite-dimensional Qp-vector space with continuous Galois action.
constructed_objects.constructed: The underlying Q5-vector space of the E-line.
constructed_objects.justification: The representation used by Tate is this restriction of scalars, not an incorrectly assumed Q5-valued character.

index_domain_coverage.required: All inertia elements and a nonempty local-unit neighborhood in the local algebraicity conclusion.
index_domain_coverage.constructed: The entire character restriction is semisimple; the theorem supplies an open subgroup of local units.
index_domain_coverage.justification: No finite list of units is substituted for the open-subgroup assertion.

transition_maps.required: Local reciprocity and an algebraic torus morphism.
transition_maps.constructed: G_m maps to GL_Q5(E) and then to Res_E/Q5 G_m because it commutes with E on a Zariski-dense open subgroup.
transition_maps.justification: Weil-restriction adjunction identifies this morphism with an integral power; the inverse in Serre reciprocity agrees with the cyclotomic unit convention.

consumed_object_identity.required: The actual twisting character is finite order times an integral cyclotomic power.
consumed_object_identity.constructed: The power comes from the algebraic map; the quotient has finite inertia at5 and at the other finitely many ramified primes.
consumed_object_identity.justification: Class field theory over Q factors the quotient through a finite ray-class group, so it is the same global character up to that power.

coefficient_conventions.required: Q5-linear Hodge-Tate condition and Serre local reciprocity convention.
coefficient_conventions.constructed: Finite E/Q5 coefficients; manuscript Tate convention assigns cyclotomic weight-1.
coefficient_conventions.justification: The argument tracks the inverse on local units and only then compares weight multisets; it does not assume identical sign notation in Serre.

local_conditions.required: Finite base field over Qp, local algebraicity only near1.
local_conditions.constructed: Q5 satisfies the source hypotheses. Other local inertia groups are addressed through local class field theory and the pro-l/pro-5 argument.
local_conditions.justification: Finitely many ramified places allow one finite global conductor. The real place is included in the ray modulus when needed.

exceptional_cases.required: No assertion for nonabelian representations or infinite coefficient fields; negative powers allowed.
exceptional_cases.constructed: The twisting character is abelian and defined over a finite coefficient extension; the integral power can have either sign.
exceptional_cases.justification: The surrounding proof establishes its deRham property separately; that premise is retained rather than inferred from this theorem.

downstream_consumption.required: The modular twist becomes finite after matching the two Hodge-Tate weights.
downstream_consumption.constructed: The existing weight comparison forces weight2 and zero cyclotomic exponent; the finite Dirichlet character is absorbed into the eigenform.
downstream_consumption.justification: The replacement supplies exactly the character classification used there. Modularity, weight comparison, Shimura and Li inputs remain separately inventoried.
